question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about index options traded in India?

answer.text: The underlying asset is a market index like Nifty 50 or Sensex, and final settlement is in cash
The underlying asset is individual stocks from the index, and settlement is by physical delivery
Index options are only available in American style in India
Index options can only be traded by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)

explanation.text: The Logic: Index options have a stock index — such as Nifty 50, Sensex, or Bank Nifty — as the underlying. Because an index cannot be physically delivered, the final settlement of index options in India is in cash. The Trap: Index options in India are European style, not American, and they are open to all categories of investors — not restricted to FIIs. Note: Stock options, by contrast, settle by physical delivery of the underlying shares at expiry.
